parameters.rationale: CRED-02 fingerprint similarity threshold (§7.2, §13.2). Starting hypothesis, unvalidated at v0.1.
CRED-04 minimum redirect-hop count (§7.2: "redirect hops ≥ 2"). Value taken directly from the frozen predicate text.
PM-01 page-age threshold below which a permission request is considered unsolicited (§7.2, §13.2). Starting hypothesis.
§9.4 Medium-tier lower bound (Warn). Value taken directly from the frozen threshold table.
§9.4 High-tier lower bound (Block). V-6 checks no primary rule's baseWeight reaches this value alone.
G-03 store-write fingerprint collision guard (§13.2, §20.6). Independent from tau_sim by design (DEC-10) — must not be assumed equal.
§20.4 PROVISIONAL → ESTABLISHED establishment threshold N (authentication count).
§20.4 PROVISIONAL → ESTABLISHED establishment threshold M (distinct days).
A-01 user-trust validity period (§6.4, §13.2): trust SHALL expire.

refinementSets.rationale: R-02 (§5.3) executable/archive membership list — native executables and installers, script and shortcut formats, and archive containers commonly used to wrap them. Draft starting list; exact membership is a versioned rule-set artifact per §5.3.

R-03 (§5.4) sensitive-permission membership list. Mirrors the closed SensitivePermission enum already frozen in evidence.contract.v1.ts — PermissionContextFindings.requestedPermission cannot report a value outside this set, so this list documents rather than independently gates that boundary.

S-02 (§6.3) federated identity provider registry. §6.3: no authoritative machine-readable IdP registry exists; curated list, small in practice. Exact-string-equality only — never substring, suffix, or similarity (§6.3).

rules.name: Off-origin credential post
rules.rationale: Detects credentials destined for a registrable domain other than the one the user believes they are visiting — the canonical structural signature of credential harvesting. Distinguished from CRED-05 (script-mediated exfiltration, invisible to this predicate) and CRED-04 (cross-site arrival without off-site submission).
knownFalsePositiveRisks: Federated authentication not covered by the S-02 registry
Embedded payment and identity iframes
Multi-brand corporate estates operating a shared authentication domain across regional TLDs
knownLimitations: Cannot observe submission destinations rewritten by script at submit time — that case belongs to CRED-05. A page may declare a benign action attribute and override it dynamically.

rules.name: Unfamiliar impersonation
rules.rationale: The page structurally and visually resembles a login page the user has genuinely authenticated to, on a domain where they never have — the platform's strongest zero-hour signal, derived from the individual user's own history rather than any external blocklist. No other rule reads the Authentication History Store.
knownFalsePositiveRisks: White-label and shared-template platforms where many legitimate tenants render near-identical login pages
A user's first visit to a legitimate regional or sibling property of a site they already use
knownLimitations: Cold start — no protection until the user has authenticated at least once. A stale fingerprint following a legitimate site redesign causes a false negative, not a false positive, mitigated by refreshing the stored fingerprint on every successful authentication and retaining the two to three most recent per origin.

rules.name: Deceptive identity with credential collection
rules.rationale: Visual domain deception is only weakly meaningful alone; this rule is the only one that requires it to co-occur with active credential collection, distinguishing deceptive-but-benign IDN sites from deceptive sites actively harvesting credentials.
knownFalsePositiveRisks: Legitimate internationalized domains in non-Latin scripts — material in non-English markets, SHALL be measured on a regionally representative negative set, not solely a Latin-script one.
knownLimitations: Requires a confusables/skeleton mapping. Single-script non-Latin domains are legitimate and common; the rule SHOULD weight mixed-script representation more heavily than non-ASCII representation alone.

rules.name: Laundered arrival
rules.rationale: Credential collection reached through a multi-hop cross-site redirect chain is characteristic of link-laundering through compromised or disposable intermediaries — the only rule keying on redirect-chain shape rather than the landing page's own properties.
knownFalsePositiveRisks: Advertising networks, link shorteners, marketing campaign tracking
Legitimate SSO chains, which routinely produce multi-hop cross-site redirects
knownLimitations: Hop counting reflects only what the extension observes; server-side redirect chains may be collapsed before the extension sees them, understating the true count.

rules.name: Script-mediated credential exfiltration
rules.rationale: Captures credentials leaving the page by script rather than by form submission, to an off-site endpoint — the exfiltration path CRED-01 structurally cannot see, since CRED-01 only reads the form's declared action, not runtime script behavior.
knownFalsePositiveRisks: Analytics instrumentation attached to form fields
Password strength meters
Single-page applications authenticating against an API on a different registrable domain
knownLimitations: Reliable observation requires instrumentation established before page scripts execute. Dynamically constructed or obfuscated endpoints may evade endpoint attribution.

rules.name: Cleartext credential collection
rules.rationale: Credentials collected over an unencrypted transport are exposed regardless of the site's intent — the only rule keying purely on transport security, independent of destination or script behavior.
knownFalsePositiveRisks: Local development environments
Legacy intranet applications
Captive portals
knownLimitations: Increasingly rare on the public web, and browsers already surface their own warning. Retained because it is unambiguous and cheap; its empirical contribution may prove small.

rules.name: Concealed credential collection
rules.rationale: Concealment of credential collection combined with off-site submission — the only rule triggered by field-level concealment (hidden or autocomplete-disabled) rather than by transport, destination pattern, or visual deception alone. Carries the lowest primary weight and requires the off-site conjunct to fire at all.
knownFalsePositiveRisks: Password manager integration fields
Financial institutions that disable autocomplete as a matter of policy
knownLimitations: Weak in isolation, which is why it carries the lowest primary weight and requires the off-site conjunct to fire at all.

rules.name: Injected credential interface
rules.rationale: INTERPRETIVE CHOICE, FLAGGED FOR REVIEW: §7.2 states this aggravator's parent requirement as "CRED-01 or CRED-02" (two possible parents), but RuleDefinition.parent is singular (RuleId | null) and §9.2/§9.3's aggregation model is likewise single-parent. CRED-01 was chosen as the sole parent — not derived from spec text, an explicit judgment call pending architect ruling. Consequence: this aggravator will NOT contribute when only CRED-02 (not CRED-01) is present, narrowing §7.2's literal 'or' behavior. Client-side injection of a credential interface from an off-site script is meaningful as corroboration and meaningless alone — this is why it carries no standalone weight.
knownFalsePositiveRisks: Essentially the entire modern single-page-application web — component frameworks routinely inject login forms post-load from bundled or CDN-hosted scripts. This is precisely why the rule carries no standalone weight.
knownLimitations: Attribution of the injecting script's origin is not always reliable where bundlers rewrite or inline sources.

rules.name: Suspicious executable delivery
rules.rationale: Executable content delivered cross-site from a page already carrying security findings — the only rule requiring a pre-existing finding on the referring session, which is what makes flagging routine cross-site CDN delivery tolerable at all. priorFindingActive reads committed prior-pass state only (§7.2 interpretation, v0.7), never the in-flight finding set, keeping aggregation pure (§9.1).
knownFalsePositiveRisks: Legitimate CDN- and release-host-delivered installers, which are cross-site by normal practice. The requirement for a pre-existing finding on the referring session is what makes this rule tolerable at all.
knownLimitations: Requires referring session context; a download initiated by direct navigation has no referring page and cannot match. No file content inspection is performed or claimed — this is delivery-context analysis only. A download initiated before any Tier 0/1 finding exists cannot match — intended behaviour, not a defect.

rules.name: Deceptive file typing
rules.rationale: Type deception corroborates suspicious delivery — the only rule reading declared-extension/MIME consistency, distinguishing an intentionally mistyped file from an ordinarily-typed one at an otherwise-suspicious delivery.
knownFalsePositiveRisks: Servers emitting generic octet-stream content types
Legitimate archives with compound extensions
knownLimitations: Declared content types are frequently generic, limiting how often the inconsistency test can conclude anything.

rules.name: Unsolicited sensitive permission
rules.rationale: A sensitive capability requested without user initiation, on a page reached indirectly or only just loaded — the only rule evaluating permission-request context; no other rule reads PermissionContext at all.
knownFalsePositiveRisks: Conferencing and mapping applications that request capabilities immediately on load as a matter of design.
knownLimitations: User gesture attribution is imprecise across frames and asynchronous handlers. The page-age threshold is empirical (§13.2).

suppressions.purpose: Users legitimately re-authenticate to familiar sites constantly. Treating routine re-authentication as anomalous would make the product unusable.
suppressions.rationale: INTERPRETIVE NARROWING, FLAGGED FOR REVIEW: §6.2's guard is stated as three conditions — origin_present=true, lifecycleState=ESTABLISHED, AND fingerprint drift within tolerance. No ParameterId exists for a drift-tolerance threshold (checked against the full §13.2 tunable list; 'drift tolerance' has no corresponding entry), so the third condition cannot be expressed as a guard Predicate. This guard checks only origin_present and lifecycleState=ESTABLISHED, treating drift-within-tolerance as already folded into the module's own ESTABLISHED determination rather than independently re-checked at Stage 2. This is a real narrowing of §6.2's literal three-condition wording, not a full implementation of it.

suppressions.purpose: Federated authentication involves credential submission in the context of a third-party identity provider. Registry-listed providers are exempted from off-origin post penalties.
suppressions.rationale: Without the CRED-03 guard, an attacker registering a confusable lookalike of a registry entry would obtain automatic exemption from the strongest credential rule (§6.3). Registry match is by exact string equality only — never substring, suffix, or similarity.

changeLog.summary: Initial rule set: eleven rules (nine primary, two aggravator), eleven parameters, three refinement sets, empty subsumption table (§10.4). TWO of THREE §6 suppressions included (S-01, S-02); A-01 (User-Trusted Origin) is OMITTED. Checked exhaustively across every module contract, not just the two most obviously relevant ones: no field anywhere represents a per-origin explicit user trust action. D0.8's lifecycleState is authentication-derived (repeated logins over time), architecturally distinct from A-01's "explicit, recorded user trust action" (a single deliberate click past a warning). Sharper framing of the gap: trust_validity_days IS a defined, frozen ParameterId (ruleset_format_v1.ts:70, tagged // A-01) — the spec froze A-01's tunable parameter without ever providing anywhere for its underlying guard data to live. §6.1 forbids an unguarded suppression ("A suppression without guards is an exploitable bypass"), and no V-check enforces non-empty guards, so shipping A-01 with guards: [] would be a silent, uncaught violation of a frozen architectural invariant. Needs either an evidence-contract amendment adding the missing evidence category, or confirmation that user-trust suppression is handled entirely outside the rule-set predicate mechanism.

DEFECT-15 fix, authorized by Jayanth (Architecture Owner). CRED-01, CRED-02, CRED-07, and CRED-A1 each compared against loginForm.pageRegistrableDomain, which is permanently null — LoginInterfaceEvidence carries no page-domain field, so this module cannot report one (see loginForm.ts's header comment and DEFECT-15). All four notSameSite comparisons were permanently vacuous as a result. Swapped the right-hand operand to url.registrableDomain (a real, evidence-grounded field — DEFECT-16 names this as a recurring pattern, first hit by CRED-05/CRED-06 at v0.1.0 authoring) and added url to each rule's requiredModules, appended at the position matching that rule's existing first-appearance-order convention (verified per rule, not assumed). Predicate meaning changed for four rules — MINOR per §14.1, not PATCH. Each rule's lastModifiedIn bumped to 0.2.0 accordingly. Nothing else changed: same eleven rules, eleven parameters, three refinement sets, two suppressions, empty subsumption table. integrityDigest recomputed using the newly-committed tools/ci/compute-ruleset-digest.mjs (SHA-256 over canonical JSON, sorted keys, integrityDigest blanked before hashing — see that file's header for the exact algorithm); its --verify mode confirms this file's stored digest against a fresh recomputation.
